must_identify.item: The pod is Pending with FailedScheduling Insufficient cpu
must_identify.evidence: Every node in the cluster has only 10 allocatable CPUs [7, 8], so no node could ever satisfy this request, producing the FailedScheduling event "0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu" [6].

must_identify.item: The cause is the 64-core CPU request, above any node's allocatable CPU
must_identify.evidence: The root cause was a resource misconfiguration introduced in the worker Deployment's revision 2 rollout: the new pod template requested cpu: "64" (64 whole CPU cores) instead of a millicore value [6, 9]. Every node in the cluster has only 10 allocatable CPUs [7, 8], so no node could ever satisfy this request

notes: The fix appears only in passing ('correct the resource request or roll back the deployment', plus kubectl set resources / rollout undo under Not Checked) and never names 50m explicitly. A rollback would still restore the 50m request. The taint in the event is quoted but not blamed, and the claim of an out-of-band edit is an inference from the last-applied annotation, not a confirmed fact.
